notes: Assertions grade repo-first validation, selective direct-copy versus optional plugin delivery, purpose preservation, report-only live-config recommendations, and the registry/pricing contract. The model-change case exercises scripts/lib/checks.py model_crosscheck against an explicit settings.defaults.claude.model; Claude best is exempt. Registration is consistency rather than liveness proof. Registered Claude IDs also need an exact scripts/pricing.toml entry with all four rates. Runtime pricing matches an exact ID or a date-suffixed variant and returns $0 when unmatched; an older minor model is not a pricing fallback. Pricing-coverage independently requires exact registered entries. Prompts are inline research/plan requests and authorize no tool calls or live changes.

evals.name: modernize-claude-setup
evals.prompt: Answer inline in at most 300 words; do not enter plan mode or run tools. Use this frozen 2026-09-21 review instead of claiming fresh research: the khenrix-quality and khenrix-writing skill triggers need clearer wording, the optional Claude plugin help text has an outdated model recommendation, and the live Claude default may need tuning. State how you would improve this machine's setup, validate the repo changes, deliver each changed surface, and handle the live default. Nothing has been applied yet.
assertions: Edits the khenrix-utils repo (the directory with capabilities.toml / .git), NOT an installed copy, and validates from that repo with `mise run verify`

Chooses delivery by changed surface: `khenrix-quality`, `khenrix-writing`, their provenance/selective settings, or house-style use the reviewed `skills:plan` / content-addressed `skills:apply` / `skills:doctor` path plus the Maka smoke; optional plugin or broader rendered content uses `make khenrix-refresh`; a change touching both uses both paths

Separates changes into two buckets: repo edits applied with confirmation, vs live-config tuning that is only recommended (never auto-applied); does not invent a specific replacement model without verified evidence
Preserves each skill's purpose — improves wording/structure/triggering/model usage, not the behaviour a skill delivers
Plans to write a dated report under docs/upgrades/ with findings and copy-paste live-config commands

evals.name: model-change-is-recommendation-only
evals.prompt: Answer inline without running tools. This is a hypothetical migration of a machine whose checked-out `capabilities.toml` still pins `[settings.defaults.claude].model = "claude-opus-5"` (the fixture is not a claim about this branch's current default). A frozen 2026-09-24 official-source review verifies `claude-opus-5-5` as the recommended model for this setup; after a reviewed repo edit, `mise run defaults:apply` backs up the live config and aligns only declared default leaves. State how you would switch this hypothetical machine, including what you would apply to the repo and what you would only recommend for live config. Do not run commands or claim a switch happened.
assertions: Treats the live model change as a recommendation: puts the exact copy-paste command `mise run defaults:apply` in the dated report rather than executing it

Uses the supplied dated research evidence to recommend `claude-opus-5-5` for this hypothetical machine and does not replace it with an unverified model guess or claim to have performed new live research
Distinguishes the repo-side change to `[settings.defaults.claude].model` in `capabilities.toml` (applied with confirmation) from the report-only live command in `docs/upgrades/claude-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`

evals.name: introducing-a-model-id-touches-two-manifests-or-it-breaks
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. In a hypothetical reviewed migration, I have changed `capabilities.toml` `[settings.defaults.claude].model` from the dynamic `best` alias to a newly verified explicit Claude model ID. That ID has no entry yet in `[models].claude` or `scripts/pricing.toml`. What else in khenrix-utils has to change before this is safe to commit, what does the actual defaults crosscheck validate, and what breaks if I skip registration or pricing? Nothing has been applied to live config.
assertions: Says the explicit Claude default must be REGISTERED in `capabilities.toml` `[models].claude`; `scripts/lib/checks.py` model_crosscheck validates `settings.defaults.*.model` against each provider registry, exempts Claude's dynamic `best` alias, and makes `make verify` fail for this unregistered explicit default

Requires an exact model-ID entry in `scripts/pricing.toml` with input, output, cache_read and cache_write rates; pricing-coverage makes `make verify` fail if a registered Claude ID lacks its exact entry; an unmatched runtime price lookup otherwise silently reports $0

Explains that scripts/claude_session_stats.py price() matches an exact ID or a date suffix (-YYYYMMDD or @YYYYMMDD), never a new minor version or approximate neighbour; an unmatched ID silently returns $0, so an older model rate does not replace the required exact entry

Does not treat changing the declared default alone as sufficient, claim that model_crosscheck validates a removed engine table or arbitrary fanout profile, or treat registry membership as fresh model availability proof; live config remains a report-only recommendation
